af.overview: A rugged landlocked nation known as the "graveyard of empires." It has been at war almost continuously since 1979.
af.wars: Anglo-Afghan Wars (1839–1919); Soviet–Afghan War (1979–89); Civil War (1992–96); US-led war (2001–21)
af.notable: The Taliban retook power in August 2021 after the US withdrawal.

al.overview: A Balkan nation that spent decades under the isolated communist rule of Enver Hoxha. It joined NATO in 2009.
al.wars: Italian invasion (1939); World War II resistance; Kosovo War spillover (1999)
al.notable: Dotted with hundreds of thousands of Cold War bunkers.

dz.overview: Africa's largest country by area. It won independence from France in 1962 after a brutal eight-year war, then endured a bloody civil war in the 1990s.
dz.wars: Algerian War of Independence (1954–62); Sand War with Morocco (1963); Algerian Civil War (1991–2002)
dz.notable: Hosts huge Saharan oil and gas fields; the FLN became a model for anti-colonial movements.

ad.overview: A tiny Pyrenean co-principality between France and Spain.
ad.notable: Famous for the myth of its "war on Germany" that supposedly lasted until 1958.

ao.overview: A former Portuguese colony that became independent in 1975 and was instantly split by a Cold War proxy civil war lasting until 2002.
ao.wars: War of Independence (1961–74); Civil War (1975–2002); interventions in Congo
ao.notable: Cuban and South African troops fought large battles here; now a major oil producer.

ag.overview: A twin-island Caribbean nation, independent from Britain since 1981. It has no major war history.
ag.notable: Nelson's Dockyard was a major Royal Navy base.

ar.overview: South America's second-largest country by area, shaped by Spanish rule, European immigration and military dictatorships.
ar.wars: Independence Wars (1810–18); War of the Triple Alliance (1864–70); Falklands War (1982)
ar.notable: The 1982 loss to Britain helped topple the military junta.

am.overview: An ancient Caucasus nation and the first state to adopt Christianity (301 AD). It has fought repeated wars with Azerbaijan.
am.wars: First Nagorno-Karabakh War (1988–94); Second (2020); 2023 Azerbaijani offensive

au.overview: A continent-sized nation that has fought alongside Britain and the US in nearly every major conflict.
au.wars: World Wars I and II; Korean War; Vietnam War; Gulf War; Afghanistan (2001–21); Iraq
au.notable: The Gallipoli landing in 1915 is a defining national moment.

at.overview: The heart of the Habsburg Empire, once one of Europe's great powers. Now a neutral republic.
at.wars: War of the Spanish Succession (1701–14); Napoleonic Wars; Austro-Prussian War (1866); World War I (1914–18)
at.notable: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand sparked WWI.

az.overview: A Caspian oil nation that retook Nagorno-Karabakh in 2020 and 2023.
az.notable: Oil boom began in Baku in the 1800s.

bs.overview: A Caribbean archipelago, independent from Britain since 1973.

bh.overview: A small island monarchy in the Persian Gulf hosting the US Fifth Fleet.
bh.notable: Led the Gulf's pearl trade historically.

bd.overview: A densely populated delta nation that broke away from Pakistan in 1971.
bd.notable: Born from a war in which millions fled to India.

bb.overview: A small, stable Caribbean island nation. It became a republic in 2021.
bb.notable: Former sugar colony; birthplace of Rihanna.

by.overview: A former Soviet republic and close ally of Russia, ruled by Alexander Lukashenko since 1994.
by.wars: World War II (about a quarter of the population died); allowed Russian forces to stage the 2022 invasion of Ukraine
by.notable: Hosts Russian forces and Russian tactical nuclear weapons.

be.overview: A small but strategic nation twice overrun by Germany in the 20th century. It hosts the EU and NATO headquarters.
be.wars: Belgian Revolution (1830); World Wars I and II; Congo wars (colonial)
be.notable: Occupied in 1914 and 1940; King Leopold's Congo brutality is a dark legacy.

bz.overview: Central America's only English-speaking nation, formerly British Honduras.
bz.notable: Home to the world's second-largest barrier reef.

bj.overview: Home of the old Dahomey kingdom, famed for its elite female warriors. A French colony until 1960.
bj.notable: First African state to peacefully abandon Marxism-Leninism (1990).

bt.overview: A small Himalayan kingdom that has largely avoided wars.
bt.wars: Duar War with Britain (1864–65); Operation All Clear against Indian militants (2003)
bt.notable: Measures national success by "Gross National Happiness."

bo.overview: A landlocked Andean nation that lost its coastline in a war with Chile.
bo.wars: War of the Pacific (1879–84); Chaco War (1932–35)
bo.notable: Lost its Pacific coast to Chile, which it still disputes.

ba.overview: A Balkan nation of Bosniaks, Serbs and Croats, torn apart by war after Yugoslavia broke up.

bw.overview: A stable, diamond-rich democracy since independence from Britain in 1966. It has avoided major wars.
bw.wars: No major wars; border incursions during the Rhodesian and apartheid eras
bw.notable: One of Africa's longest-running multiparty democracies.

br.overview: South America's giant and the world's fifth-largest country by population and area.
br.wars: War of the Triple Alliance (1864–70); World Wars I and II (fought in Italy)
br.notable: The only South American nation to send troops to WWII combat.

bn.overview: A tiny, oil-rich sultanate on Borneo, once a great regional power.
bn.notable: One of the world's wealthiest nations per capita.

bg.overview: A Balkan nation that has fought several wars to gain territory.
bg.wars: Balkan Wars (1912–13); World Wars I and II
bg.notable: Fought on the losing side in both world wars.

bf.overview: A landlocked Sahel state that has seen repeated coups. It now faces a serious jihadist insurgency.
bf.wars: Agacher Strip War with Mali (1974, 1985); jihadist insurgency (2015–)
bf.notable: Thomas Sankara's radical revolution (1983–87); several coups since 2014.

bi.overview: A small Central African state scarred by Hutu–Tutsi ethnic violence since independence in 1962.
bi.notable: Peace agreements in 2000 and 2005 ended the worst of the fighting.

cv.overview: An Atlantic island nation that won independence from Portugal in 1975 and has been peaceful since.
cv.wars: Part of the PAIGC liberation struggle (1963–74)
cv.notable: A stable democracy that was once a hub of the Atlantic slave trade.

kh.overview: Heart of the Khmer Empire that built Angkor Wat. It endured one of the 20th century's worst genocides.
kh.wars: Cambodian Civil War (1967–75); Khmer Rouge genocide (1975–79); Cambodian–Vietnamese War (1977–91)
kh.notable: The Khmer Rouge killed about a quarter of the population.

cm.overview: A former German, then British and French, colony. It now faces separatist and jihadist violence.
cm.wars: Bakassi border dispute with Nigeria (1990s); Boko Haram conflict (2014–); Anglophone Crisis (2017–)
cm.notable: The only African state with both British and French colonial legacies.

ca.overview: The world's second-largest country by area, with a small but professional military.
ca.wars: War of 1812; World Wars I and II; Korean War; Gulf War; Afghanistan (2001–14)
ca.notable: The Battle of Vimy Ridge (1917) is a defining national moment.

cf.overview: A resource-rich but extremely poor country gripped by repeated coups and civil wars.
cf.notable: Hosts UN peacekeepers and foreign mercenary forces.

td.overview: A vast Sahel country that has known near-constant rebellion since independence from France in 1960.
td.wars: Chadian–Libyan conflict (1978–87); civil wars; Boko Haram conflict
td.notable: Won the 1987 "Toyota War," routing Libya's army with armed pickup trucks.

cl.overview: A long, narrow Andean country that won major territory in the War of the Pacific.
cl.wars: War of the Pacific (1879–84); Independence Wars

cn.overview: An ancient civilisation that rose from civil war and foreign occupation. It has the largest army by personnel.
cn.wars: Opium Wars (1839–60); Sino-Japanese Wars (1894–95, 1937–45); Civil War (1927–49); Korean War (1950–53); Sino-Indian War (1962); Sino-Vietnamese War (1979)
cn.notable: Invented gunpowder, paper and the compass; tested nuclear weapons from 1964.

co.overview: A South American nation riven by decades of guerrilla and drug-cartel violence.
co.wars: La Violencia (1948–58); conflict with FARC and ELN (1964–2016); Korean War
co.notable: The 2016 peace deal ended the war with FARC.

km.overview: A small island nation off Mozambique, independent from France since 1975 and notorious for coups.
km.wars: No major wars; around 20 coups or attempts since 1975
km.notable: Mercenary Bob Denard staged several coups here.

cg.overview: A French-colonial oil state that suffered civil wars in the 1990s.
cg.notable: Known as Congo-Brazzaville to separate it from its giant neighbour.

cr.overview: A peaceful Central American democracy that abolished its army in 1948.
cr.wars: Costa Rican Civil War (1948); no standing army since
cr.notable: Rare example of a nation with no military.

ci.overview: Once West Africa's stable showcase economy, then split by civil war.

hr.overview: A Balkan country on the Adriatic that won independence from Yugoslavia in 1991.
hr.wars: Croatian War of Independence (1991–95); World War II

cu.overview: A Caribbean island ruled by a communist government since the 1959 revolution.
cu.wars: Cuban War of Independence (1895–98); Revolution (1953–59); Bay of Pigs (1961); Angolan intervention (1975–91)
cu.notable: The 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis nearly caused nuclear war.

cy.overview: An island divided since the 1974 Turkish invasion.
cy.notable: The UN Green Line splits the capital.

cz.overview: A Central European nation formed from Bohemia and Moravia. It was occupied twice in the 20th century.
cz.wars: Thirty Years' War (began in Prague, 1618); World Wars I and II; Soviet invasion (1968)
cz.notable: The Prague Defenestration of 1618 helped start the Thirty Years' War.

cd.overview: A giant, mineral-rich state ravaged by the deadliest conflict since World War II.
cd.wars: Congo Crisis (1960–65); First Congo War (1996–97); Second Congo War (1998–2003); M23 conflict in the east (2012–)
cd.notable: The Second Congo War drew in nine nations and killed millions.

dk.overview: A small Scandinavian kingdom whose Vikings once raided much of Europe.
dk.wars: Viking conquests; Napoleonic Wars; Second Schleswig War (1864); WWII occupation (1940–45); Gulf, Iraq, Afghanistan
dk.notable: Lost to Prussia in 1864 and was occupied by Germany in 1940.

dj.overview: A tiny Horn of Africa state on the Red Sea chokepoint. It hosts bases of the US, France, China and others.
dj.wars: Civil War (1991–94); border clash with Eritrea (2008)
dj.notable: Strategic location on the Bab-el-Mandeb strait.

dm.overview: A mountainous Caribbean island nation, independent from Britain since 1978.
dm.notable: Last Caribbean island colonised by Europeans, thanks to fierce Carib resistance.

do.overview: Shares Hispaniola with Haiti. It declared independence from Haiti in 1844.
do.wars: War of Independence (1844); Restoration War (1863–65); US occupation (1916–24); Civil War (1965)
do.notable: The 1965 civil war prompted US intervention.

ec.overview: An Andean country straddling the equator. Long border tensions with Peru.
ec.notable: Lost a large share of its territory to Peru in 1941.

eg.overview: An ancient civilisation of pharaohs and the most populous Arab state. It has fought Israel several times and made peace in 1979.
eg.wars: Arab–Israeli Wars (1948, 1956, 1967, 1973); North Yemen Civil War (1962–70); Libyan–Egyptian War (1977)
eg.notable: Controls the Suez Canal; first Arab state to recognise Israel (1979).

sv.overview: A small Central American state, scarred by a bloody civil war and gang violence.
sv.wars: Football War with Honduras (1969); Civil War (1979–92)
sv.notable: A recent crackdown on gangs sharply cut murders.

gq.overview: A small, oil-rich former Spanish colony ruled by the same family since 1979.
gq.notable: Obiang's rule makes him one of the world's longest-serving leaders.

er.overview: Won independence from Ethiopia after a thirty-year struggle. It remains a closed, heavily militarised state.
er.wars: Eritrean War of Independence (1961–91); Eritrean–Ethiopian War (1998–2000); Tigray War (2020–22)

ee.overview: A small Baltic nation that regained independence from the Soviet Union in 1991.
ee.wars: Estonian War of Independence (1918–20); Soviet occupation (1940–91)
ee.notable: A leader in e-government and a NATO member since 2004.

sz.overview: One of the world's last absolute monarchies, surrounded by South Africa and Mozambique.
sz.wars: No major wars; never fully conquered

et.overview: An ancient empire never colonised in the usual sense. It famously crushed an Italian invasion in 1896.
et.wars: Battle of Adwa (1896); Italian invasion (1935–41); Ogaden War (1977–78); Eritrean wars; Tigray War (2020–22)
et.notable: Home of the African Union headquarters; a symbol of resistance to colonialism.

fj.overview: The largest Pacific island nation after Papua New Guinea, independent since 1970.

fi.overview: A Nordic nation that held off the Soviet Union in the Winter War. It joined NATO in 2023.
fi.wars: Finnish Civil War (1918); Winter War (1939–40); Continuation War (1941–44); Lapland War (1944–45)
fi.notable: Heroic defense in the Winter War despite being heavily outnumbered.

fr.overview: From the guillotine of 1789 to Napoleon's conquest of Europe, France has risen and fallen in blood. It is a nuclear-armed power.
fr.wars: Hundred Years' War; Napoleonic Wars (1803–15); Franco-Prussian War (1870–71); World Wars I and II; Indochina (1946–54); Algeria (1954–62)
fr.notable: Napoleon redrew the map of Europe; built an independent nuclear deterrent in 1960.

ga.overview: An oil-rich, forested nation ruled by one family for over fifty years until a 2023 coup.
ga.notable: Among the richest African states per capita.

gm.overview: A sliver of land surrounding the Gambia River, entirely enclosed by Senegal.
gm.wars: 1981 coup attempt; regional intervention in 2017 to remove Jammeh
gm.notable: Peaceful transition after Yahya Jammeh's 22-year rule.

ge.overview: A Caucasus nation that lost control of two regions to Russian-backed separatists.
ge.wars: Georgian Civil War (1991–93); Abkhaz and South Ossetian wars; Russo-Georgian War (2008)
ge.notable: Russian troops remain in Abkhazia and South Ossetia.

de.overview: Unified by Prussian iron in 1871, it dragged the world into two wars. Divided by the Cold War, reunified in 1990.
de.wars: Franco-Prussian War (1870–71); World War I (1914–18); World War II (1939–45)
de.notable: The Nazi regime murdered six million Jews in the Holocaust.

gh.overview: The first sub-Saharan colony to win independence, in 1957 under Kwame Nkrumah.
gh.notable: A stable democracy and major gold and cocoa producer.

gr.overview: Birthplace of democracy and the ancient city-states of Athens and Sparta.
gr.wars: Persian Wars; Peloponnesian War; War of Independence (1821–29); Balkan Wars; Greco-Italian War (1940–41); Civil War (1946–49)
gr.notable: Resisted Italy and then Germany in WWII.

gd.overview: A small Caribbean island nation independent from Britain since 1974.
gd.notable: The 1983 US-led invasion followed a Marxist coup.

gt.overview: The largest Central American nation by population. A long civil war devastated its Mayan communities.
gt.notable: The civil war left an estimated 200,000 dead.

gn.overview: Rejected French rule in 1958. It has been dominated by strongmen and coups since.
gn.wars: Spillover from Sierra Leone and Liberian wars
gn.notable: Rich in bauxite and iron ore.

gw.overview: A small West African state with a history of coups, drug trafficking and political instability.
gw.notable: Amílcar Cabral led the independence struggle.

gy.overview: South America's only English-speaking nation, now an oil boomtown.
gy.notable: Venezuela claims about two-thirds of its territory.

ht.overview: The world's first Black republic, won by a slave revolt against France in 1804.
ht.wars: Haitian Revolution (1791–1804); US occupation (1915–34); gang insurgency (2020s)
ht.notable: Toussaint Louverture led the world's only successful slave revolution.

va.overview: The world's smallest state and seat of the Catholic Church.
va.wars: No modern wars; Swiss Guard has defended the Pope since 1506
va.notable: Has been a UN observer state since 1964.

hn.overview: A Central American nation that fought a short war with El Salvador over a football match.
hn.notable: US used Honduras as a base during the Cold War.

hu.overview: Once a great power in the Austro-Hungarian Empire. It lost two-thirds of its territory after WWI.
hu.wars: Mongol invasion (1241); Ottoman wars; World War I; World War II; Hungarian Revolution (1956)
hu.notable: The 1956 uprising against Soviet rule was crushed by tanks.

is.overview: A North Atlantic island nation with no army. It was settled by Vikings.
is.notable: The Cod Wars were fought with fishing boats and nets, not guns.

in.overview: Independent from Britain since 1947 and now the most populous nation on Earth. A nuclear power facing Pakistan and China.
in.wars: Indo-Pakistani Wars (1947–48, 1965, 1971); Sino-Indian War (1962); Kargil War (1999)
in.notable: Won independence through mass civil disobedience; tested nuclear devices in 1974 and 1998.

id.overview: The world's largest archipelago and most populous Muslim-majority nation.
id.wars: Indonesian National Revolution (1945–49); Konfrontasi with Malaysia (1963–66); East Timor occupation (1975–99); Aceh insurgency (1976–2005)
id.notable: Anti-communist purge of 1965–66 killed hundreds of thousands.

ir.overview: Heir to the ancient Persian Empire, transformed by the 1979 Islamic Revolution. It projects power through the Revolutionary Guard and allied militias.
ir.wars: Iran–Iraq War (1980–88); proxy conflicts across the region; missile exchanges with Israel (2024); 12-day war with Israel (2025)
ir.notable: Suffered chemical weapons attacks from Iraq.

iq.overview: Land of ancient Mesopotamia and Babylon, fought over in modern times.
iq.wars: Iran–Iraq War (1980–88); Gulf War (1991); US invasion (2003–11); war against ISIS (2014–17)

ie.overview: A republic that fought for centuries against English and British rule.
ie.wars: Nine Years' War (1594–1603); Irish Rebellion (1798); War of Independence (1919–21); Civil War (1922–23)

il.overview: Founded in 1948 after the Holocaust, surrounded by hostile neighbours. It has a highly capable military and mandatory draft.
il.wars: 1948 War; Suez Crisis (1956); Six-Day War (1967); Yom Kippur War (1973); Lebanon Wars (1982, 2006); Gaza war (2023–)
il.notable: Rescued hostages at Entebbe (1976); widely believed to hold undeclared nuclear weapons.

it.overview: Heir to the Roman Empire, unified only in 1861.
it.wars: Roman conquests; Italian Wars of Independence; World Wars I and II; Italo-Turkish War (1911–12)
it.notable: Mussolini's Fascist regime allied with Nazi Germany.

jm.overview: A Caribbean island nation, independent from Britain since 1962.
jm.notable: Birthplace of reggae and Bob Marley.

jp.overview: A land of samurai that modernised in one generation and built an empire. It was crushed in 1945 and now keeps a pacifist constitution.
jp.wars: Sino-Japanese Wars (1894–95, 1937–45); Russo-Japanese War (1904–05); World War II (1941–45)
jp.notable: Hit by atomic bombs in 1945; Article 9 renounces war.

jo.overview: A desert kingdom bordering Israel, Iraq, Syria and Saudi Arabia.

kz.overview: The world's largest landlocked country, a former Soviet republic and nuclear-weapons renouncer.
kz.notable: Gave up the Soviet nuclear arsenal it inherited in the 1990s.

ke.overview: East Africa's economic hub, born from a brutal fight against British rule.
ke.wars: Mau Mau Uprising (1952–60); Shifta War (1963–67); war on al-Shabaab in Somalia (2011–)
ke.notable: Hosts a large Nairobi diplomatic and tech scene.

ki.overview: A scatter of Pacific atolls straddling the equator and the date line.
ki.notable: One of the nations most threatened by sea-level rise.

kw.overview: A small oil-rich emirate invaded by Iraq in 1990.

kg.overview: A mountainous Central Asian republic that has seen two revolutions since 2000.
kg.wars: Tulip Revolution (2005); ethnic clashes (2010); border war with Tajikistan (2021–22)

la.overview: A landlocked communist state and the most heavily bombed country per capita in history.
la.wars: Laotian Civil War (1959–75); Vietnam War spillover
la.notable: The US dropped more bombs on Laos than it did on Germany and Japan combined in WWII.

lv.overview: A Baltic nation that regained independence from the Soviet Union in 1991.
lv.wars: Latvian War of Independence (1918–20); WWII occupation
lv.notable: Joined NATO and the EU in 2004.

lb.overview: A Mediterranean nation of many faiths, shattered by civil war.
lb.wars: Lebanese Civil War (1975–90); Israeli invasions (1982, 2006); 2024 Israel–Hezbollah war
lb.notable: The 2020 Beirut port explosion killed over 200.

ls.overview: A mountain kingdom completely surrounded by South Africa.
ls.notable: The Basotho kept their independence through diplomacy and mountain defence.

lr.overview: Founded by freed American slaves in 1847, it was torn apart by civil war.
lr.notable: Charles Taylor was convicted of war crimes in 2012.

ly.overview: An oil-rich North African state that fell into chaos after Gaddafi was overthrown in 2011.
ly.wars: Italo-Turkish War (1911); Chadian–Libyan conflict (1978–87); Libyan Revolution (2011); Civil Wars (2014–20)

li.overview: A tiny Alpine principality between Switzerland and Austria with no army.
li.notable: Legend says its 80-man army returned from the 1866 war with 81 men.

lt.overview: A Baltic nation that was once a vast medieval empire.
lt.wars: Battle of Grunwald (1410); Lithuanian Wars of Independence (1918–20); Soviet occupation
lt.notable: Was the first Soviet republic to declare independence (1990).

lu.overview: A small, wealthy grand duchy in Western Europe.
lu.wars: Occupied in World Wars I and II
lu.notable: Founding member of the EU and NATO.

mg.overview: A huge island nation with unique wildlife and a history of French colonial rule.
mg.notable: Home to species found nowhere else on Earth.

mw.overview: A landlocked, densely populated nation on a great African lake.
mw.notable: Sometimes called "the warm heart of Africa."

my.overview: A multi-ethnic federation in Southeast Asia, formed in 1963.
my.notable: The Malayan Emergency defeated a communist insurgency.

mv.overview: A low-lying island chain in the Indian Ocean, independent from Britain since 1965.
mv.notable: Among the countries most threatened by sea-level rise.

ml.overview: Heart of the medieval Mali Empire, now battling jihadists and rebels in its north.
ml.wars: Tuareg rebellions (1962–64, 1990s, 2012); jihadist insurgency (2012–); Agacher Strip War (1974, 1985)
ml.notable: Mansa Musa of Mali was among the richest people in history.

mt.overview: A Mediterranean island nation, long a strategic naval fortress.
mt.wars: Great Siege of Malta (1565); Siege of Malta (1940–42)
mt.notable: Awarded the George Cross for its WWII heroism.

mh.overview: A Pacific atoll nation used for US nuclear tests.
mh.wars: WWII Pacific campaign; US nuclear tests (1946–58)

mr.overview: A Saharan state straddling Arab and sub-Saharan Africa.
mr.wars: Western Sahara War (1975–79); Senegal border conflict (1989)
mr.notable: Last country in the world to abolish slavery (1981, criminalised 2007).

mu.overview: An Indian Ocean island fought over by the French and British.
mu.wars: Battle of Grand Port (1810); no major wars since independence in 1968
mu.notable: A stable democracy and tourism hub.

mx.overview: Heir to the Aztec empire and Spain's richest colony. It lost half its territory to the United States.
mx.wars: Independence War (1810–21); Mexican–American War (1846–48); French intervention (1861–67); Revolution (1910–20); cartel war (2006–)
mx.notable: Lost California, Nevada, Utah and much more in the 1848 treaty.

fm.overview: A scattering of Pacific islands in free association with the US.
fm.notable: Chuuk Lagoon holds a graveyard of Japanese warships.

md.overview: A small former Soviet republic with a breakaway region, Transnistria.

mc.overview: A tiny Mediterranean principality known for wealth and the Grand Prix.

mn.overview: Birthplace of Genghis Khan's empire, the largest contiguous land empire in history.

me.overview: A Balkan nation that regained independence from Serbia in 2006.
me.wars: Balkan Wars (1912–13); World War I; Yugoslav Wars (1990s)

ma.overview: An old kingdom that was a French and Spanish protectorate until 1956.
ma.wars: Rif War (1921–26); Sand War (1963); Western Sahara War (1975–91)
ma.notable: Controls most of the disputed Western Sahara.

mz.overview: Portuguese colony that gained independence in 1975 and then suffered a long civil war.
mz.wars: War of Independence (1964–74); Civil War (1977–92); Cabo Delgado insurgency (2017–)

mm.overview: A former British colony in Southeast Asia, ruled by the military for most of its modern history.
mm.wars: Anglo-Burmese Wars (1824–85); Civil War (1948–); Rohingya crisis (2017); post-coup war (2021–)

na.overview: Former German colony and later South African-ruled territory. It became independent in 1990.
na.wars: Herero and Nama genocide (1904–08); Independence struggle (1966–90)
na.notable: Germany has formally acknowledged the genocide.

nr.overview: The world's smallest island nation, once enriched by phosphate mining.

np.overview: A Himalayan nation home to Mount Everest, never colonised by Britain.
np.notable: Gurkha soldiers serve in the British and Indian armies.

nl.overview: A low-lying seafaring nation that built a global trading empire.
nl.wars: Eighty Years' War (1568–1648); Anglo-Dutch Wars; Napoleonic Wars; WWII occupation; Indonesian independence war
nl.notable: Dutch Golden Age made it a major world power.

nz.overview: A Pacific nation that has fought in both World Wars as a loyal ally of Britain.
nz.wars: New Zealand Wars (1845–72); World Wars I and II; Korean War; Vietnam War
nz.notable: The ANZAC legend was born at Gallipoli in 1915.

ni.overview: A Central American nation shaped by US interventions and the Sandinista revolution.
ni.notable: Sandinistas toppled the Somoza dictatorship in 1979.

ne.overview: A vast Sahel country that is one of the poorest on Earth. It was taken over by the military in 2023.

ng.overview: Africa's most populous nation and largest economy.
ng.wars: Biafran War (1967–70); Boko Haram insurgency (2009–); ECOWAS interventions in Liberia and Sierra Leone
ng.notable: The Biafran War killed up to a million or more.

kp.overview: A hermit state ruled by the Kim dynasty since 1948. It is technically still at war with the South.
kp.wars: Korean War (1950–53; armistice only); Pueblo seizure (1968); reported troops to aid Russia (2024–)

mk.overview: A Balkan nation that gained independence from Yugoslavia in 1991.

no.overview: A Nordic kingdom whose Vikings explored the North Atlantic.
no.wars: Viking conquests; WWII invasion (1940); Gulf and Afghan deployments
no.notable: Norwegian resistance sabotaged the Nazi heavy-water plant.

om.overview: A historic seafaring sultanate on the Arabian Sea.
om.notable: Known for neutrality and mediation in regional disputes.

pk.overview: Carved out of British India in 1947 and locked in rivalry with India ever since. A nuclear-armed state.
pk.wars: Indo-Pakistani Wars (1947–48, 1965, 1971); Kargil War (1999); insurgency on Afghan border (2001–)
pk.notable: Lost East Pakistan (now Bangladesh) in 1971; became a nuclear power in 1998.

pw.overview: A tiny Pacific nation with an ancient culture.
pw.notable: One of the bloodiest Pacific WWII battles took place here.

ps.overview: A territory comprising the West Bank and Gaza Strip, recognised as a state by many UN members.
ps.wars: Arab–Israeli Wars; First Intifada (1987–93); Second Intifada (2000–05); Gaza war (2023–)
ps.notable: A non-member observer state of the UN.

pa.overview: Famed for the Panama Canal, finished by the US in 1914.
pa.notable: The 1989 US invasion deposed Manuel Noriega.

pg.overview: A large Pacific nation with hundreds of languages.
pg.wars: Kokoda Track campaign (1942); Bougainville Civil War (1988–98)
pg.notable: Kokoda is a defining Australian WWII battle.

py.overview: A landlocked nation that was nearly destroyed in the nineteenth century.
py.wars: War of the Triple Alliance (1864–70); Chaco War (1932–35)
py.notable: Lost most of its adult male population in the Triple Alliance War.

pe.overview: Heart of the Inca Empire, later Spain's main South American colony.
pe.wars: War of the Pacific (1879–84); Ecuadorian–Peruvian wars (1941, 1995); Shining Path insurgency (1980–2000)
pe.notable: Shining Path's insurgency killed about 70,000 people.

ph.overview: A Southeast Asian archipelago colonised by Spain, then the US, then occupied by Japan.
ph.wars: Philippine Revolution (1896–98); Philippine–American War (1899–1902); World War II; Moro insurgency (1969–2014)
ph.notable: Battle of Manila (1945) devastated the capital.

pl.overview: A Central European nation repeatedly partitioned and invaded. It was the first victim of WWII.
pl.wars: Polish–Soviet War (1919–21); German invasion (1939); Warsaw Uprising (1944)
pl.notable: Lost about six million citizens in World War II.

pt.overview: A small seafaring nation that pioneered European exploration. It built a global empire.
pt.wars: Age of Discovery; Peninsular War; Colonial Wars (1961–74); World War I
pt.notable: The 1974 Carnation Revolution ended a dictatorship and its colonial wars.

qa.overview: A tiny gas-rich emirate with enormous wealth, hosting a major US air base.

ro.overview: A Balkan state with the legend of Vlad the Impaler.
ro.wars: World Wars I and II; Romanian Revolution (1989)

ru.overview: The largest country on Earth, heir to the Tsars and the Soviet Union. It holds the biggest nuclear arsenal.
ru.wars: Napoleon's invasion (1812); Civil War (1917–22); Great Patriotic War (1941–45); Soviet–Afghan War (1979–89); Chechen Wars; Georgia (2008); Ukraine (2014–)
ru.notable: Lost about 27 million Soviet citizens in WWII; launched Sputnik and Gagarin.

rw.overview: A small, densely populated Central African nation, site of the 1994 genocide.
rw.wars: Rwandan Civil War (1990–94); 1994 genocide (about 800,000 killed); invasions of Congo (1996–)
rw.notable: Rebuilt rapidly under Paul Kagame's rule.

kn.overview: The smallest country in the Americas by area and population.
kn.notable: Brimstone Hill Fortress is a UNESCO site.

lc.overview: A volcanic Caribbean island that changed hands between Britain and France many times.
lc.wars: No major wars; contested by Britain and France (1600s–1814)

vc.overview: A Caribbean island nation, independent since 1979.
vc.notable: Garifuna people, of African and Carib descent, resisted British rule here.

ws.overview: A Polynesian island nation, independent since 1962 from New Zealand.
ws.notable: First Polynesian nation to regain independence in the 20th century.

sm.overview: The world's oldest surviving republic, enclaved in Italy.

st.overview: A tiny two-island nation in the Gulf of Guinea, independent from Portugal since 1975.

sa.overview: Home to Islam's holiest sites and the world's largest oil exporter.
sa.notable: Founded in 1932 after Ibn Saud unified the Arabian peninsula.

sn.overview: A relatively stable West African democracy and former French colonial hub.
sn.notable: Dakar was the terminus of the Dakar Rally for years.

rs.overview: The core of the former Yugoslavia, repeatedly at war in the 1990s.
rs.wars: Balkan Wars (1912–13); World War I; Yugoslav Wars (1991–99); Kosovo War (1998–99)
rs.notable: Archduke Franz Ferdinand's assassin was Serbian.

sc.overview: An Indian Ocean island nation, independent from Britain since 1976.

sl.overview: A West African state devastated by an 11-year civil war.
sl.notable: Notorious for "blood diamonds" and child soldiers.

sg.overview: A wealthy island city-state that split from Malaysia in 1965.
sg.notable: The fall of Singapore in 1942 was Britain's worst military defeat in Asia.

sk.overview: A Central European nation that split peacefully from Czechoslovakia in 1993.
sk.wars: World War II; Slovak National Uprising (1944)

si.overview: The first Yugoslav republic to break away, in 1991.

sb.overview: A Melanesian island nation where some of WWII's fiercest fighting occurred.
sb.notable: Guadalcanal was a turning point in the Pacific War.

so.overview: A Horn of Africa nation without a fully functioning central government since 1991.
so.wars: Ogaden War (1977–78); Civil War (1991–); Battle of Mogadishu (1993); al-Shabaab insurgency (2006–)
so.notable: The "Black Hawk Down" battle took place in Mogadishu.

za.overview: Africa's most industrialised nation, shaped by Zulu kings, Boer settlers and British imperialism. Apartheid ended in 1994.
za.wars: Anglo-Zulu War (1879); Boer Wars (1880–81, 1899–1902); World Wars I and II; South African Border War (1966–90)
za.notable: Developed nuclear weapons in secret, then dismantled them.

kr.overview: Rebuilt from the ruins of the Korean War into an industrial giant. A conscript army guards the DMZ.
kr.wars: Korean War (1950–53); Vietnam War (about 300,000 troops); Yeonpyeong shelling (2010)

ss.overview: The world's youngest nation, independent since 2011 and soon thrown into civil war.
ss.wars: Second Sudanese Civil War (1983–2005); South Sudanese Civil War (2013–20)
ss.notable: Has large oil reserves but severe poverty.

es.overview: Once the greatest empire in the world, ruling vast territory in the Americas.
es.wars: Reconquista; Spanish Armada (1588); Peninsular War (1808–14); Spanish–American War (1898); Spanish Civil War (1936–39)
es.notable: The Civil War killed an estimated 500,000 people.

lk.overview: An island nation off India, devastated by a 26-year civil war.
lk.notable: The Tamil Tigers pioneered suicide-bombing tactics.

sd.overview: A vast northeast African nation shattered by decades of civil war.
sd.wars: Civil Wars (1955–72, 1983–2005); Darfur conflict (2003–); army–RSF war (2023–)
sd.notable: Split in two in 2011 when South Sudan seceded.

sr.overview: A former Dutch colony on South America's north coast.
sr.notable: Only Dutch-speaking nation in South America.

se.overview: A Nordic nation that was once a major European military power.
se.wars: Thirty Years' War; Great Northern War (1700–21); Napoleonic Wars (last war, 1814)
se.notable: Has stayed out of war since 1814.

ch.overview: A neutral Alpine nation that has avoided war for over two centuries.

sy.overview: One of the world's oldest inhabited regions, wrecked by a civil war that began in 2011.
sy.notable: The Assad regime fell in December 2024.

tj.overview: A mountainous former Soviet republic in Central Asia.
tj.wars: Tajik Civil War (1992–97); border war with Kyrgyzstan (2021–22)
tj.notable: Over 90% of the country is mountainous.

tz.overview: Formed in 1964 by the union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar, led by Julius Nyerere.
tz.notable: Invaded Uganda and toppled Idi Amin in 1979.

th.overview: The only Southeast Asian nation never colonised by a European power.
th.wars: Franco-Thai War (1940–41); World War II (allied with Japan); Cambodia border clashes
th.notable: Has a long record of military coups.

tl.overview: A small half-island nation that won independence from Indonesia in 2002.
tl.notable: Occupation killed around a quarter of the population.

tg.overview: A narrow West African state, German then French colony until 1960.
tg.notable: Ruled by the Gnassingbé family since 1967.

to.overview: The last Polynesian kingdom, never colonised.
to.notable: Never formally colonised by a European power.

tt.overview: A twin-island nation and Caribbean energy producer.

tn.overview: Site of ancient Carthage and Hannibal's empire. It sparked the 2011 Arab Spring.
tn.notable: The Arab Spring began with the Tunisian Revolution of 2010–11.

tr.overview: Heart of the old Ottoman Empire, reborn as a republic under Atatürk in 1923. It has NATO's second-largest army.
tr.wars: Gallipoli (1915); War of Independence (1919–23); Korean War (1950–53); invasion of Cyprus (1974); Kurdish PKK conflict (1984–)
tr.notable: Controls the straits linking the Black Sea and Mediterranean.

tm.overview: A reclusive, gas-rich former Soviet republic.

tv.overview: A tiny Pacific nation with a very small population.

ug.overview: A landlocked East African nation, infamous for the brutal rule of Idi Amin in the 1970s.
ug.wars: Uganda–Tanzania War (1978–79); Bush War (1981–86); LRA conflict (1987–2006); interventions in Congo
ug.notable: The LRA became known for abducting child soldiers.

ua.overview: A large Eastern European nation that has been fought over for centuries.
ua.wars: Ukrainian War of Independence (1917–21); World War II; Russo-Ukrainian War (2014–)
ua.notable: Gave up Soviet nuclear weapons in the 1990s.

ae.overview: A federation of seven emirates, rich in oil and finance.
ae.notable: Home to Dubai and Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building.

gb.overview: A small island that built the largest empire in history. It is a nuclear power and a founding NATO member.
gb.wars: Hundred Years' War; Napoleonic Wars; Crimean War; Boer Wars; World Wars I and II; Falklands War (1982); Iraq and Afghanistan
gb.notable: Stood alone against Hitler in 1940; cracked Enigma at Bletchley Park.

us.overview: A superpower born from the 1776 revolt against Britain. It has the largest military budget on Earth and is the only nation to use nuclear weapons in war.
us.wars: American Revolution (1775–83); Civil War (1861–65); World Wars I and II; Korean War; Vietnam War; Gulf War; Afghanistan (2001–21); Iraq (2003–11)
us.notable: Built the atomic bomb, landed on the Moon in 1969 and led NATO through the Cold War.

uy.overview: A small South American democracy sandwiched between Brazil and Argentina.
uy.wars: Guerra Grande civil war (1839–51); War of the Triple Alliance (1864–70)
uy.notable: Won the first World Cup in 1930.

uz.overview: Heart of the old Silk Road and home of Timur's (Tamerlane's) empire.
uz.wars: Uzbek–Tajik border tensions; Afghan conflict spillover

vu.overview: A Melanesian archipelago governed jointly by Britain and France before independence.
vu.notable: Famous for land diving (the origin of bungee jumping).

ve.overview: An oil-rich nation that led the independence of northern South America under Simón Bolívar.
ve.wars: Independence Wars (1810–23); Federal War (1859–63); border dispute with Guyana
ve.notable: Home to the world's largest proven oil reserves.

vn.overview: A Southeast Asian nation that defeated France and the United States in turn.
vn.wars: First Indochina War (1946–54); Vietnam War (1955–75); Cambodian–Vietnamese War (1977–89); Sino-Vietnamese War (1979)
vn.notable: Victory at Dien Bien Phu (1954) ended French rule.

ye.overview: The poorest nation in the Arabian peninsula, broken by civil war.
ye.wars: North Yemen Civil War (1962–70); Civil War (1994); Houthi–Saudi war (2015–)
ye.notable: One of the world's worst humanitarian crises.

zm.overview: A copper-rich nation that hosted anti-apartheid and liberation movements.
zm.wars: No major wars; support for liberation struggles
zm.notable: Kenneth Kaunda led it from 1964 to 1991.

zw.overview: Formerly Rhodesia, it won independence in 1980 after a long guerrilla war.
zw.wars: Rhodesian Bush War (1964–79); Gukurahundi (1980s); Second Congo War (1998–2003)
zw.notable: Hyperinflation devastated its economy in the 2000s.
